Definition: Jabbok, a river east of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Jacob rose up that night and took his two wives and his eleven sons and passed over the ford Jabbok. Israel smote Sihon and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Jabbok is the river of the turning point: Jacob crosses it on the night he wrestles and is renamed, and Israel's border runs to it because the river marks where the wandering ends and the land begins.
